# Setup and workflow

**Board:** NUCLEO-H533RE (STM32H533RET6, Cortex-M33, 512 KB flash, 272 KB RAM).

**Tools (Windows):** STM32CubeMX, CMake, Ninja, Docker Desktop, VS Code. The compiler and
STM32_Programmer_CLI are taken from the folder `C:\ST\STM32CubeIDE_1.18.0` (IDE not opened) by `scripts/env.ps1`.

**Project:** `bms_h5/` is generated by CubeMX from `bms_h5/bms_h5.ioc` (CMake toolchain, FreeRTOS from the
X-CUBE-FREERTOS pack). Re-generate after changing pins/peripherals; our code lives in `USER CODE` blocks and in `bms_h5/App/`.

Pin map (from the .ioc):

| Pin | Use |
|---|---|
| PA2 / PA3 | USART2 TX/RX = ST-LINK virtual COM port (`/dev/ttyACM0` on the Jetson) |
| PA5 | LD2, green user LED (the only user LED on this Nucleo) |
| PB2 / PC2 / PC1 | SPI2 SCK / MISO / MOSI, for the W5500 Ethernet module (not used yet) |
| PB12 / PA8 / PC9 | W5500 SPI_CS / RSTN / INTN (not used yet) |

**Build:** `.\scripts\build.ps1` (or VS Code: Ctrl+Shift+B). Output: `bms_h5/build/Debug/bms_h5.elf` and `.bin`.

**Flash, board on this laptop:** `.\scripts\flash_local.ps1`

**Flash, board on the Jetson:** `JETSON=user@host ./scripts/deploy_jetson.sh` (Git Bash). It copies the `.bin` onto
the Nucleo's ST-LINK USB drive (`NOD_H533RE`), which flashes the board. No OpenOCD needed (the apt version doesn't support STM32H5).
Edit the `JETSON` value in `.vscode/tasks.json` to use the VS Code task.

`docs/reference/h5-latest.ioc` is the team's custom BMS board (STM32H523CE) CubeMX file, kept for reference only. It is not built.
